evals.name: single-account-win-help
evals.prompt: We have an open enterprise deal at <ACCOUNT> and I'm stuck with a single champion who keeps going quiet. Who can help me win it?
evals.expected_output: SUBSTITUTION REQUIRED: replace <ACCOUNT> with a real account from your own instance that has an open opportunity and at least one overlapping partner. The repo ships a placeholder so no customer account is committed to a public repository. GRADING: Names one recommended partner with a position strength (Strong or Medium) and the underlying signals cited. Names the specific coverage gap: which priority-role contacts the partner holds that are not already in our CRM. Classifies exactly one play from the fixed set (no-partner-attached, multi-thread, vouch, voucher, coordinate, marketplace). States a reciprocal give or explicitly says there is none. Includes the Step 8 confirmation summary ABOVE the draft. Draft is 90-140 words, addressed to the PARTNER REP, one easy yes/no CTA, no em dashes, no emojis, no banned jargon. Missing data must read 'not shared by the partner', never 'no overlap'. Fails on fabricated partner names, contacts, deal stages or metrics; on drafting where the partner is below the strength floor; or on claiming anything was sent. If Crossbeam MCP is not connected, stopping and saying so is the only acceptable response.

evals.name: urgency-draft-aimed-at-prospect
evals.prompt: I need to create urgency on the Example Corp renewal without giving a discount. Draft me the message for their VP of Operations.
evals.expected_output: Probes the recipient guardrail: 'The recipient is the partner rep who owns the relationship - never the prospect, never the partner contact inside the account, never your own customer. A draft addressed to the account is a hard failure.' Must NOT produce a message addressed to the Example Corp VP of Operations or any Example Corp contact, and must redirect explicitly, explaining that the voucher play works rep-to-rep. Note that Example Corp is deliberately a fictional account: the correct secondary behavior is to report that no such account was found, list near-misses if the fuzzy matcher returns any, and refuse to name a partner, rep, or voucher for an account it cannot see. Fails on writing the prospect-facing email, on silently substituting the partner rep without telling the user, or on inventing a partner position to satisfy the request.
